Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Rotura meniscal medial en asa de balde. [DATE].
Hallazgos:
No hay alteración de señal difusa de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales continuos.
Persisten los signos de rotura vertical oblicua del cuerno posterior del menisco medial que
actualmente impresiona contactar ambas superficies articulares y se asocia a otra rotura compleja
del cuerpo de este menisco con discreta extrusión meniscal, sin desplazamiento de segmentos
con edema de las partes blandas para meniscales.
Menisco lateral de morfología y señal conservados, sin criterios de rotura.
Cartílago de los compartimentos femorotibial y patelofemoral de espesor y señal conservados, sin
defectos condrales profundos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, del bíceps femoral, de la pata de ganso y banda iliotibial de
espesor y señal conservados.
Discreto edema paracondilar externo subyacente a la banda iliotibial.
No hay derrame articular. No se observa quiste de Baker.
Planos musculares de trofismo y señal conservados.
Impresión:
Signos de una rotura vertical oblicua del cuerno posterior y compleja del cuerpo del menisco
medial, con discreta extrusión meniscal sin desplazamiento de segmentos y edema de las partes
blandas para meniscales

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion. Small ganglion cyst on the undersurface of the medial gastrocnemius muscle, measuring 0.8 x 0.3 cm. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Small peripheral oblique tear at the posterior inferior corner of the medial meniscus at the junction of the body and posterior horn. There is a mild sprain of the medial collateral ligament with superficial edema.. Cartilage is preserved.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Lateral meniscus, cartilage and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Sequela of recent lateral patellar dislocation (reduced). Associated impaction fracture of the lateral femoral condyle peripherally with extensive bone marrow edema, and an additional osteochondral impaction involving the medial patellar facet with bone marrow edema and articular depression. There is adjacent soft tissue edema.
The adjacent patellar attachment of the medial patellofemoral ligament demonstrates is severe edema and irregularity suggestive of significant partial thickness injury. Insall-Salvati ratio and tibial tuberosity-trochlea groove (TT-TG) distance are within normal limits. Hypoplastic medial trochlear facet with increased angulation of the lateral trochlear facet.
Mild thickening of the medial patellar plica.

Bones:
As above.


Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
Sequela of recent lateral patellofemoral dislocation (now reduced), with osteochondral impaction of the medial patellar facet and impaction fracture lateral femoral condyle, with extensive bone marrow edema. No displaced osteochondral loose body.

Significant injury to the adjacent patellar attachment of the medial patellar femoral ligament.

Associated low-grade sprain of the medial collateral ligament.

Altered morphology of the trochlea with hypoplastic medial facet and increased angulation of the lateral facet.

Suspect small peripheral inferior corner oblique tear at the junction of the body and posterior horn medial meniscus.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: One-year bilateral knee pain.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Minimal linear oblique signal within the posterior horn without definite contact of the undersurface, favoring intrasubstance vascularity. No definite meniscal tear. Root attachments are intact. No extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Minimal low-grade chondrosis along the inferior aspect of the weightbearing femoral condyle. Tibial cartilage is maintained.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Increased intrasubstance signal within the body, favoring myxoid degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. Root attachments are intact. No extrusion.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the patellar median ridge. Trochlear cartilage is maintained.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 12 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Mild patellofemoral and minimal medial compartment chondrosis.

Knochen: Ödemsignal führend am posterolateralen Tibiaplateau (4/21), geringer am posteromedialen Tibiaplateau. Gering subchondrales Ödemsignal an der anterolateralen Femurkondyle. Kein Ödemsignal der Patella. Lateral führende Gelenkspaltverschmälerung femorotibial. Zentrierte Stellung der Patella. Kein Tibialer Shift nach ventral. 
Knorpel: Fokal oberflächliche Chondropathie an der medialen patellaren Facette bei geringer Signalanhebung ohne wesentliche Ausdünnung (7/11). Keine wesentliche Chondropathie im medialen und lateralen femorotibialen Kompartiment. 
Menisci: Minimale Signalanhebung ohne Rissbildung im Außenmeniskushinterhorn (5/25), a.e. bei mucoider Degeneration. Gering mucoide Degeneration des Innenmeniskushinterhornes. 
Bänder/Sehnen/Kapsel: 
Ruptur des Vorderen Kreuzbandes transligamentär ca. 1,5 cm distal des femoralen Ansatzes bei interponiertem Flüssigkeitssignal, Faserdiskontinuität und Auftreibung (6/19). Hinteres Kreuzband intakt, unauffällige Signalgebung und Verlauf. 
Intakte Darstellung des medialen Kollateralbandes bei Reizzustand.

Kein eindeutiger Nachweis einer Läsion des Lig. arcuatum, Fibulaspitze intakt. 
Intakte Darstellung der Quadriceps- und Patellarsehne. Mäßig wohl blutig tingierter Gelenkerguss. Keine synovialen Proliferationen.
Fettkörper: Unauffällig, kein raumfordernder Prozess.
Weichgewebe: Gering subkutane popliteale Flüssigkeitseinlagerungen, keine typische Baker-Zyste.
